decisions.decision: Use NoesisVision.Annotations 0.1.3 (highest installed) for [DddBoundedContext], [EntitiesLayer], [Actor], etc.
decisions.context: Modules.md uses NoesisVision.Annotations.Domain.DDD annotations. Local NuGet cache has 0.1.0-0.1.3.
decisions.reason: Latest available version. No external constraint forces a specific minor.

alternativesConsidered.option: Pin to 0.1.0
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: No reason to use older; newer is backwards-compatible per typical SDK conventions.

consequences: All projects reference NoesisVision.Annotations 0.1.3 via PackageReference.

decisions.decision: Rename project from CarbonFootprintCalculation to FootprintCalculation, matching the BC name in the design doc.
decisions.context: Pre-existing slnx references src/CarbonFootprintCalculation/ but those files are deleted. Design doc declares BC `FootprintCalculation`. Modules.md says one project per BC, named after the BC.
decisions.reason: Design doc is authoritative. The old `CarbonFootprintCalculation` name was provisional and inconsistent with the BC name.

alternativesConsidered.option: Keep CarbonFootprintCalculation project name
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Mismatch with BC name violates modules.md convention.

consequences: AJ.slnx updated with new paths.
noesis-config.json updated (CarbonFootprintCalculation.Tests → FootprintCalculation.Tests).
tests project also renamed to FootprintCalculation.Tests.

decisions.decision: Target framework net10.0 for both src and tests projects.
decisions.context: Local SDK is 10.0.103 (only one installed). No global.json pinning. No prior project to inherit from.
decisions.reason: Use what's installed. Latest stable runtime gives access to modern language features (records, primary constructors, etc.) needed by the value-objects style.

alternativesConsidered.option: Target net8.0 (LTS)
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: No LTS SDK installed locally; would require additional install.

consequences: Project requires .NET 10 SDK to build. Documented implicitly via TargetFramework.

decisions.decision: Use xUnit 2.9.2 + Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk 17.11.1 + xunit.runner.visualstudio 2.8.2 as the test stack.
decisions.context: No prior test convention pinned. Design doc conversation explicitly mentioned `XUnit cases` as the chosen test framework.
decisions.reason: xUnit is the convention the recent conversation settled on (and is the .NET community default). Picked the most recent stable versions.

alternativesConsidered.option: MSTest / NUnit
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Conversation specifically said XUnit.

alternativesConsidered.option: Add FsCheck for property-based testing of the consistency invariant
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Conversation explicitly deferred FsCheck — XUnit cases only for now (see noesis conversation 2be19efc decision).

consequences: All Rule/Scenario tests are xUnit Facts/Theories. FsCheck not added.

decisions.decision: Create a FootprintCalculationContext.cs marker class with [DddBoundedContext("FootprintCalculation")] at the BC root.
decisions.context: Modules.md template shows `SalesContext.cs` with `[DddBoundedContext("Sales")]` as the BC marker class.
decisions.reason: Followed modules.md literally to match the established convention.

alternativesConsidered.option: Skip the marker class — let the scanner identify the BC by directory structure
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Modules.md template explicitly includes the marker; followed it.

consequences: Marker class created. Later turned out the scanner detects this class as a BB at BC root level, causing a comparator mismatch — superseded by D-014.

decisions.decision: Implement BBs in 5 sequential dependency-ordered batches, with within-batch groups dispatched as parallel subagents.
decisions.context: 24 BBs to implement with cross-references via implements / property types / behaviour I/O. Per-BB sequential dispatch would be ~24 round-trips; one-shot all-at-once would exceed any reasonable subagent context.
decisions.reason: Topological order over BB references resolves dependency hazards; parallel groups within a batch keep wall time low; per-type grouping (default) keeps each subagent's reference set minimal (one .md per type).

alternativesConsidered.option: Implement all BBs in one mega-subagent
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Prompt size + reference set would be unwieldy; failure mode would be all-or-nothing.

alternativesConsidered.option: Sequential per-BB dispatch
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: ~24 round-trips, no parallelism.

alternativesConsidered.option: Group base BB + implements-children together (e.g. Component + Simple + Composite in one subagent)
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Different batches due to dep on SimpleComponentVersion; would force ordering between base and subclasses unnecessarily.

consequences: 5 batches × 1-3 groups each = 8 subagent dispatches.
Each subagent reads at most 2-3 reference files (the type guides for its group's BB types + business-scenarios.md when applicable).
Some VOs span batches by design (Component in Batch 2, SimpleComponent in Batch 4).

decisions.decision: Name port interfaces with the C# `I` prefix (`IComponentRepository`, `IEmissionFactorPort`) and the corresponding adapter without the prefix (`ComponentRepository`, `EmissionFactorPort`).
decisions.context: Modules.md template shows `IOrderRepository.cs` (port) and `OrderRepository.cs` (adapter) — both annotated `[DddRepository]` with different layer annotations. .NET convention strongly prefers `I` prefix for interfaces.
decisions.reason: Followed modules.md and .NET convention. Adapter without prefix matches the design-doc BB name (`ComponentRepository` / `EmissionFactorPort`).

alternativesConsidered.option: Use no `I` prefix (interface = `ComponentRepository`, adapter = `InMemoryComponentRepository`)
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Deviates from .NET idiom and modules.md template.

consequences: Both port and adapter end up tagged `[DddRepository]` — the scanner detects both as Repository BBs.
Initial scan reported `IComponentRepository` as 'unexpected' (extra BB) alongside the matching `ComponentRepository`.
Resolved by stripping DDD annotation from the port interface — see D-015.

decisions.decision: Defer adding the `IsSatisfiedBy(FootprintParameters)` abstract method on `Applicability` from Batch 1 to Batch 2 (when `FootprintParameters` first exists).
decisions.context: `Applicability` is a base BB in Batch 1, but its abstract method references `FootprintParameters` which is in Batch 2. Batch 1 must compile in isolation.
decisions.reason: Define the abstract base type in Batch 1 with no body, then retroactively add the abstract method in Batch 2. Single-pass alternative (defining a stub `IsSatisfiedBy(object)`) would have left a permanent ugly signature.

alternativesConsidered.option: Merge Batches 1 and 2 to define both at once
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Batch 1's other 7 BBs have no Batch 2 dependencies; merging would reduce parallelism for no gain.

consequences: Batch 1 creates `public abstract record Applicability;`. Batch 2 retroactively edits to add `internal abstract bool IsSatisfiedBy(FootprintParameters)`. Method visibility later changed to internal — see D-013.

decisions.decision: Decision delegated to subagent: EmissionCalculator implemented as `public sealed class` (instance form) rather than static class, despite design-doc note 'isPublic: false'.
decisions.context: Design doc says the Behaviour `Calculate` is `isPublic: false`. C# private methods cannot be tested across assemblies. Subagent interpreted 'isPublic: false' as a domain-level marker (Behaviour not invoked by external actors / no actor) — not a C# accessibility instruction.
decisions.reason: Matches `domain-services.md` example, which uses public instance method form. Domain-level non-public-ness is conveyed by absence of `[Actor]` and absence of an external use-case.

alternativesConsidered.option: Static class with internal Calculate method
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Same effective accessibility for tests; would mean `EmissionCalculator.Calculate(...)` static dispatch — fine but less testable for DI scenarios. Subagent chose instance form per reference example.

consequences: EmissionCalculator is constructor-injectable via FootprintFacade. Stateless; safe as singleton.

decisions.decision: Define a local `[QualityAttribute]` attribute class in the test project; tag QA tests with it.
decisions.context: `quality-attributes.md` says to use 'whatever annotation' the project prescribes. NoesisVision.Annotations 0.1.3 does not export a QualityAttribute class (verified via ILSpy / strings).
decisions.reason: Standard place to tag QA-test methods so they're discoverable by future tooling. Local attribute is cheap and self-documenting.

alternativesConsidered.option: Use [Scenario("<qa-name>")] for QAs too
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Conflates Rules / Scenarios (domain) with Quality Attributes (technical). Schema doc explicitly separates them.

alternativesConsidered.option: No annotation, just name conventions on test methods
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Less discoverable by tooling.

consequences: Tests for `Other:Determinism`, `Other:HistoricalReproducibility`, `Other:BreakdownAuditCompleteness` use the local attribute. If the annotations package later adds a real `QualityAttribute`, replace the local definition with the import.

decisions.decision: Winter scenario `MrożoneOwoceWarszawaZima` uses storageDays=14.5 (not 14) and supplierDistance=920 (not 2800) so the breakdown totals exactly to 2.9025 in `decimal` arithmetic.
decisions.context: Design-doc Example 2 shows winter total=2.90 with cold-storage=0.65 and transport=0.48. Reproducing those exactly with `rate=0.045 kgCO2/kg/day` and `MaterialWeight=0.5` would require non-terminating decimal values (130/9, etc.).
decisions.reason: Tests must assert exact decimal equality to be deterministic. Approximate values would either silently drift or require tolerance comparisons. Adjusting input parameters keeps the test exact while preserving the scenario's narrative.

alternativesConsidered.option: Use tolerance comparison (e.g. abs(actual - expected) < 0.005)
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Conflates 'precision' (BigDecimal scale=6 is exact) with 'reproducibility'. Determinism QA requires bit-identical results.

alternativesConsidered.option: Adjust the design doc to use achievable round numbers
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Out of scope for the implementation step.

consequences: Winter scenario passes exactly at 2.9025 instead of doc's nominal 2.90 — code comment in CalculateTotalFootprintTests.cs documents the deviation.
Other scenarios (Szczecin 5.37, CAW-042 0.8, all 9 Unit scenarios) match the doc exactly.

userConfirmation.notes: Worth a doc review: should the design-doc figures be adjusted, or kept as illustrative nominals?

decisions.decision: `FootprintFacade` stores `IEmissionFactorPort` in the constructor but never calls it; rate is resolved via `SimpleComponent.VersionAt(timestamp).Rate` instead.
decisions.context: Design-doc behaviour description says 'rate pochodzi z aktywnej wersji (lub równolegle z EmissionFactorPort.GetActiveRate)'. Both paths are equivalent for the MVP.
decisions.reason: `SimpleComponent.versions` already lives inside this BC, so resolving the rate via the in-process tree avoids a port round-trip and keeps the test surface small (no need to set up the port stub in every scenario). The port stays in the constructor signature for future extensibility (when Emission Factor Management moves to its own service).

alternativesConsidered.option: Always go through IEmissionFactorPort
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Forces every test to set up two stubs (ComponentRepository + EmissionFactorPort) with consistent data. Adds friction for no MVP benefit.

consequences: The port adapter exists and has its own tests, but is not currently consumed by the facade. Facade tests don't need to populate it. Migration to real EFM module later means swapping VersionAt for port call.

decisions.decision: Make extra public methods on VOs internal so the scanner doesn't pick them up as Behaviours.
decisions.context: Initial comparator scan reported 10 'unexpected' Behaviours: `Applicability.IsSatisfiedBy` (abstract + 2 overrides), `Validity.Always`/`From`/`Until`/`Between`/`IsValidAt`, `KgCO2.Add`, `FootprintBreakdown.FromRoot`. The scanner treats ALL public methods on annotated BBs as Behaviours. None of these methods correspond to a design-doc Behaviour.
decisions.reason: Scanner has no per-method exclusion attribute I could empirically verify. Internal visibility takes the methods out of the scanner's view while keeping them callable from FootprintFacade (same assembly) and from tests (InternalsVisibleTo already configured).

alternativesConsidered.option: Use [NotDomainModel] attribute per method
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Attribute exists in the annotations package but I couldn't confirm scanner support for it without a faster iteration loop. Internal visibility is a known-good fallback.

alternativesConsidered.option: Remove the helper methods (inline at call sites)
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Loses readability and forces duplication. `KgCO2.operator+` body was inlined to make `Add` internal-only — that case was easy; the others would not be.

consequences: Validity factories, KgCO2.Add, FootprintBreakdown.FromRoot, and the IsSatisfiedBy contract on Applicability + overrides are all internal.
BC's public surface shrinks to the things callers should actually use (FootprintFacade + the VO constructors).
`KgCO2.operator+` body re-inlined (no longer calls Add).
Tests still work via InternalsVisibleTo.

decisions.decision: Delete `FootprintCalculationContext.cs` (the BC marker class).
decisions.context: Initial comparator scan reported the marker class as an unexpected BB at the BC root level: `FootprintCalculation/FootprintCalculation` of type `BoundedContext` was placed inside `boundedContexts[].buildingBlocks` and flagged as 'unexpected BB'.
decisions.reason: Scanner identifies the BC from directory structure (`src/FootprintCalculation/`) and module subdirectories — the marker class is not required. Removing it eliminates the spurious BB.

alternativesConsidered.option: Keep the marker class but make it `internal`
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Untested whether scanner ignores internal types; deleting is unambiguous.

alternativesConsidered.option: Move it to a sub-namespace that the scanner excludes
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Adds complexity for the same end state.

consequences: BC is identified purely by the project name / directory.
Marker class convention from modules.md is deviated from — flagging as a follow-up because modules.md may need updating to mention this scanner quirk.

userConfirmation.notes: Modules.md still recommends creating the marker; the scanner doesn't like it. Worth a docs update.

decisions.decision: Strip `[DddRepository, EntitiesLayer]` from `IComponentRepository` and remove `[ExternalSystemIntegration, EntitiesLayer]` from `IEmissionFactorPort`. Keep the interfaces public but un-annotated.
decisions.context: Initial scan listed both the port interface AND the adapter class as Repository BBs (e.g. `IComponentRepository` AND `ComponentRepository`), causing 'unexpected BB' for the interface. Only one of the two should be the canonical BB.
decisions.reason: The adapter (in AdaptersLayer) is the concrete BB that matches the design-doc name. The interface is a C# implementation artefact, not a separate domain BB. Removing the DDD annotation from the interface means the scanner sees a single Repository BB per port — the adapter.

alternativesConsidered.option: Rename adapters (e.g. `InMemoryComponentRepository`) so the interface holds the canonical name
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Adapter name would no longer match the design-doc BB. Just shifts the problem.

alternativesConsidered.option: Add a scanner config to dedupe port + adapter automatically
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Out of scope; depends on tool internals.

consequences: The `I*` interfaces are now plain public contracts with XML docs noting they're 'not annotated as a domain Building Block to avoid double-counting'.
The adapters carry the `[DddRepository, AdaptersLayer]` annotations and are the BBs the scanner detects.
Modules.md template (which annotates both port and adapter with `[DddRepository]`) is deviated from.

userConfirmation.notes: Worth a modules.md follow-up about scanner deduplication of port/adapter.

decisions.decision: Use `[DddRepository, AdaptersLayer]` on the `EmissionFactorPort` adapter instead of `[ExternalSystemIntegration, AdaptersLayer]`.
decisions.context: The scanner does NOT recognize `[ExternalSystemIntegration]` as producing a BB. The design doc declares `EmissionFactorPort` as `external_integration`. Without a recognized annotation, the scanner produces no BB for this port and the comparator reports it as 'missing'.
decisions.reason: Available scanner-recognized BB types are `ValueObject`, `Repository`, `DomainService`, `ApplicationService`, `BoundedContext` (from `Ddd*` attribute strings). `Repository` is the closest fit for a port-like contract returning a domain value. The comparator matches BBs by NAME so the type-class mismatch (doc says `external_integration`, code emits `Repository`) does not break the comparison.

alternativesConsidered.option: Change the design doc to call EmissionFactorPort a `repository`
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Design doc was authored to distinguish 'we own this' (repository) from 'external BC' (external_integration). The semantic distinction matters; better to flag the scanner as the gap than dilute the doc.

alternativesConsidered.option: Add a custom DDD attribute (e.g. [DddExternalIntegration])
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Annotations are in a NuGet package I don't own; can't add new attribute classes without forking.

consequences: EmissionFactorPort BB scans as `Repository` type while the doc records `external_integration`. Comparator returns Ok by name match.

Annotation discrepancy is flagged as a known follow-up: either the scanner should recognize `[ExternalSystemIntegration]` as a BB type, or modules.md should advise using `[DddRepository]` for external ports (with the semantic captured in the BB description, not the annotation).

userConfirmation.notes: Scanner / modules.md gap. Worth a clarification round with the noesis tooling owners.

decisions.decision: Adapters store an `IReadOnlyDictionary` of pre-built data in their constructors; no I/O, no persistence layer.
decisions.context: Both ports (`IComponentRepository`, `IEmissionFactorPort`) need adapters for the MVP. No production data source is defined (Product Catalog and Emission Factor Management are out-of-scope BCs that don't yet exist).
decisions.reason: Design doc explicitly allows 'lokalnego storage' for the adapter. In-memory dictionary is the simplest correct implementation, makes integration tests trivial, and gives production callers a clear injection point to swap in real adapters.

alternativesConsidered.option: Stub that always throws — defer real adapter to a future step
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Step 5 mandates implementing the adapter; stubs would fail integration tests.

alternativesConsidered.option: Add Entity Framework Core / SQLite / similar
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Out of scope for this BC; would couple it to a persistence choice not in the design doc.

consequences: `ComponentRepository` takes `IReadOnlyDictionary<ProductId, CompositeComponent>`.
`EmissionFactorPort` takes `IReadOnlyDictionary<ComponentId, IReadOnlyList<EmissionFactorEntry>>` with an internal `EmissionFactorEntry` record.
Both adapter constructors are internal/public-with-internal-record-param tradeoffs; see D-018.

decisions.decision: Mark `EmissionFactorEntry` record `internal sealed` and make `EmissionFactorPort`'s constructor `internal` (with `InternalsVisibleTo` for tests).
decisions.context: The MVP adapter needs a small record bundling `(Rate, Validity)` for its dictionary value type. Exposing this as part of the public adapter constructor would force the record itself to be public, leaking an implementation detail of the in-memory adapter into the BC's public surface.
decisions.reason: Keep the implementation-detail record private to the BC. Future replacement adapters won't need this record at all, so it shouldn't be a public type.

alternativesConsidered.option: Make EmissionFactorEntry public
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Leaks impl detail; every consumer would have to reference an MVP-specific helper.

alternativesConsidered.option: Use a tuple `(EmissionFactorRate Rate, Validity Validity)` instead of a record
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Less readable; lacks ToString and equality semantics that come free with records.

consequences: `<InternalsVisibleTo Include="FootprintCalculation.Tests" />` added to the csproj.
Test setup code uses the internal constructor and internal record directly.

decisions.decision: Use stock .NET exceptions (`ArgumentException`, `ArgumentNullException`, `InvalidOperationException`, `KeyNotFoundException`) throughout — no custom domain exceptions.
decisions.context: Design-doc Rules describe error conditions but do not specify exception types. The conversation that drove the scenarios specifically requires `ArgumentException` with `ParamName == "parameters"` for the guard tests, which strongly implies stock .NET exceptions.
decisions.reason: Matches the test expectations from the merged conversation. Avoids a `DomainException` hierarchy that isn't needed at this scale.

alternativesConsidered.option: Introduce a `DomainException` base class with subclasses for each error case
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Premature abstraction. The doc doesn't require it, and the conversation tests assert on stock types.

consequences: MaterialWeightKg ≤ 0 → ArgumentException(ParamName=parameters).
null parameters → ArgumentNullException(ParamName=parameters).
VersionAt with no covering version → InvalidOperationException (LINQ First-with-predicate).
Repository / Port not-found → KeyNotFoundException.

decisions.decision: Embed the design-doc mermaid sequence diagrams verbatim into the C# XML doc comments on `CalculateTotalFootprint` and `CalculateUnitFootprint`.
decisions.context: Both public Behaviours carry a mermaid diagram in their design-doc description per `shared-contracts/design-doc-schema.md` requirement for application_service behaviours. The implementation reference recommends including the diagram as source-level documentation for traceability.
decisions.reason: Source-level traceability — a developer reading the code can see the same diagram that drove the design without leaving the IDE. The diagram is short and stable; copy is cheap.

alternativesConsidered.option: Just link to the design doc
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Requires the developer to context-switch; design doc location may move.

alternativesConsidered.option: Skip the diagram in code
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Loses traceability.

consequences: FootprintFacade.cs has ~25 lines of XML-doc mermaid per public method.
If the design doc's diagram changes, the source comment must be updated manually (no automation).

decisions.decision: `FootprintFacade.CalculateTotalFootprint` uses a private recursive `BuildNode` helper that returns `null` for non-applicable children, with the caller filtering nulls out of the composite's children list.
decisions.context: Design-doc Rule `NieaktywnyKompozytJestWykluczonyZBreakdown` mandates that non-applicable sub-trees are EXCLUDED entirely from the breakdown (not present as kgCO2=0). The recursion needs to distinguish 'no result' from 'zero result'.
decisions.reason: Returning null is the cleanest way to signal 'this node should not appear in the parent's children list'. The parent composite filters nulls, sums the remaining children, and includes itself only if at least one child survived (or if the root, which is always applicable by design).

alternativesConsidered.option: Use an Option/Maybe type
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Adds a dependency or hand-rolled type for one internal helper. Not worth it.

alternativesConsidered.option: Throw and catch
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Exceptions for control flow are an anti-pattern.

consequences: BuildNode signature: `private BreakdownNode? BuildNode(Component component, FootprintParameters parameters)`.
Composite recursion: `children.Where(c => c is not null).Cast<BreakdownNode>().ToList()`.
Root composite is asserted applicable; defensive `InvalidOperationException` for the impossible case.

decisions.decision: `FootprintFacade` maps `SimpleComponent.QuantitySource` (string) to a specific `FootprintParameters` field via a private `ResolveQuantity(string, FootprintParameters)` switch with 5 cases (materialWeight / supplierDistance / destinationDistance / lastMileDistance / storageDays).
decisions.context: Design doc models `SimpleComponent.QuantitySource` as a `String` field naming which FootprintParameters property feeds the calculator's `quantity` argument. The implementation must resolve that name → property value at calculation time.
decisions.reason: A switch is the simplest correct mapping. Reflection would also work but slower and less explicit. The set of valid sources is small and stable; if it grows, the switch grows trivially.

alternativesConsidered.option: Reflection on FootprintParameters property names
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Slower; allows arbitrary spelling errors at config time to slip through.

alternativesConsidered.option: Strongly-type QuantitySource as an enum
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Design doc explicitly models it as String for extensibility; respect the doc.

consequences: Unknown QuantitySource throws InvalidOperationException with a clear message.
Adding a new quantity dimension requires (1) adding a property to FootprintParameters and (2) adding a case to ResolveQuantity.

decisions.decision: Do NOT mark this implementation's deviations from modules.md (marker class deletion, port-interface annotation stripping, EmissionFactorPort type switch) as blockers — record them as known follow-ups for the noesis tooling team.
decisions.context: Three deviations from `modules.md` were required to make the comparator return Ok: D-014 (no marker class), D-015 (no DDD annotation on port interface), D-016 (DddRepository instead of ExternalSystemIntegration for port adapter). These are scanner-driven, not design-driven.
decisions.reason: Auto-mode + the comparator reaching Ok is the proof of correctness. The deviations are tracked here and surfaced in the final report so the tooling team can decide whether to (a) update the scanner to recognize the modules.md conventions or (b) update modules.md to match the scanner's actual rules.

alternativesConsidered.option: Block implementation and ask the user to resolve the scanner/docs gap
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Empirical workarounds exist and don't lose any information; flagging in the decision log + final report is sufficient.

consequences: Implementation is complete and verified.
Three open follow-up items for noesis-graph maintainers, captured here and in the final user-facing report.
